name: Stride v1.0.6 — Keyholder
body:
# Stride v1.0.6 — “Keyholder”

**Please update.** This fixes two counting bugs, one of which makes today's
number visibly wrong, and both were reported by people who took the trouble to
show us rather than uninstall. Thank you.

## Today's count no longer jumps backwards

One user recorded a video of the step count climbing and then dropping again,
every few seconds, all day. That was not their phone. It was ours.

Two parts of Stride write today's total, and they did not agree on the rules.
The step sensor wrote its own figure and only ever pushed the number up. The
Health Connect sync — which runs every few seconds while the app is open — then
recalculated the day and wrote a figure that was allowed to be *lower*. Each
undid the other, forever.

It hit you whenever Health Connect's total for today sat below what the phone
had already counted, which is why it was constant for some people and never
happened to others. Accurate step filtering could cause it a second way, by
subtracting steps taken in a vehicle from a figure those steps had never been
added to.

Both writers now work from a single shared total. Within a day, the number on
screen can only go up.

Choosing **Step source → This phone** still shows exactly what the pedometer
saw, corrections downwards included. Asking for that figure is asking for that
figure.

## The notification and Live Update pill no longer freeze after midnight

Reported as "steps work in the app but not in the notification or pill".

The background service decided which day to display once, when it started, and
never re-checked. The moment the clock passed midnight it was still showing
*yesterday's* row — which by then never changes again. The app itself works the
day out every time you open it, which is exactly why the two disagreed.

Both now follow the clock across the rollover. So does the walk-tracking
notification, and so does the date printed above your step count — which had the
same fault for the same reason, and turned up while testing this fix: the count
would reset to zero for the new day while the line above it still said
yesterday.

No steps were ever lost to this one — the stored count was right, only the
notification and pill were reading the wrong day.

## Licensing moved to a licence server

Until now Stride verified licence keys inside the app. The device limit was a
constant in the APK, the verdict was computed on the device, and a refund never
really revoked anything. All three now live on a server, which hands the app a
signed entitlement it re-checks locally.

**Keys bought before this release keep working.** They are still verified
against the store that issued them. Nothing needs re-entering, no key has been
reissued, and none will be.

- **A licence covers five devices, and a device can be released.** Settings →
  Premium → *Remove licence* now frees the seat rather than only forgetting it
  on this phone, so changing handset no longer costs a permanent slot.
- **Premium survives being offline.** The entitlement is good for 30 days
  between successful checks. A dead connection — or a bad afternoon at the
  licence provider — cannot take away something you paid for. Only a definite
  "no" does.
- **The error messages are honest.** A key that has run out of devices, a device
  released from somewhere else, and a key that genuinely isn't a key used to
  produce one identical message. They are now three, each saying what to do
  next.

New purchases go through Polar, at a one-time **$3**. That is a change of
payment processor, not of pricing model — there is still no subscription, and
nothing that was free has become paid. Plainly: Gumroad's fees were taking
between 43% and 53% of a $2 sale. At $3 through Polar the fee is roughly a sixth
of that.

---

**Download:** `Stride-v1.0.6.apk` below. Android 8.0 or newer.

Accurate step filtering is **free** and always has been — Settings → Tracking.

*This APK is built from the closed tree and includes the paid components, so it
won't match the GPLv3 source byte for byte.*

name: Stride v1.0.5 — Ghost Steps
body:
**If you are on 1.0.4, please update.** This fixes a bug in it, and it is a bug
that can add thousands of steps you never took.

Everything else in 1.0.4 — the step-source control, Health Connect write-back,
the new widget, the start/stop control on the home screen — is unchanged and
carried over. This release changes one thing.

## Accurate step filtering was not actually filtering

A user reported walking fifteen minutes to a bus stop, riding the bus to work,
and arriving with **around 17,000 steps instead of around 2,000** — with
*Accurate step filtering* switched on the whole way.

They had done nothing wrong. The setting reported itself as on while doing
nothing at all. Four separate faults, all ours:

**It stopped running and never restarted.** The activity detector that powers the
filter lives inside the background tracking service, and nothing treated the
filter itself as a reason to run that service. After a reboot, a low-memory kill,
or turning background tracking off, the detector was gone — while the switch
still read as on.

**It could only ever filter Stride's own step sensor.** If Google Fit, Samsung
Health or your phone's built-in detector logged the same bus ride into Health
Connect, those steps arrived untouched — and when Health Connect wins the day,
that is the number you see. Vibration counted during a ride is now subtracted
from whichever source wins.

**Sitting still counted as proof you had got off.** A smooth bus or train reports
"still" at high confidence for minutes at a time, which unlatched the filter
mid-journey and let the vibration back in. Only actual movement on foot clears it
now.

**Every failure was silent.** Play Services missing, the Physical activity
permission refused, the subscription rejected — each one wrote a log line nobody
would ever read and left the switch looking healthy. Settings now tells you when
the filter is not running, and what to do about it.

## Stride can tell you about updates again

You are reading this because you came looking. That was the only way to find out.

The in-app update checker was removed ahead of the planned Play Store launch,
which made sense for a Play build and no sense at all for the APK actually being
handed out on GitHub and Gumroad. 1.0.4 shipped without it, so nobody running it
would ever have learned that this release exists.

It's back, under **Settings → Updates**: check by hand, or automatically daily,
weekly or monthly, with the release notes shown before you download anything.
It's off nothing and costs nothing — set it to Never if you'd rather not.

The eventual Play build deliberately leaves it out, since Play forbids an app
updating itself outside the store and delivers updates itself.

## Everything else

No other changes. If you never used accurate step filtering, 1.0.4 and 1.0.5
behave identically for you — apart from finally being able to hear about the
next release.

---

**Download:** `Stride-v1.0.5.apk` below. Android 8.0 or newer.

Accurate step filtering is **free**, and always has been — it is in
Settings → Tracking, not behind Premium. It uses Google Play Services activity
recognition; with it off, Stride counts entirely on-device.

*This APK is built from the closed tree and includes the paid components, so it
won't match the GPLv3 source byte for byte.*

name: Stride v1.0.4 — Elevate
body:
This release raises the floor: a count that can't go backwards, a source you
choose rather than one imposed on you, steps that flow out to your other health
apps, and a widget worth putting on a home screen.

## Step source

`Settings → Health Connect → Step source`

| Mode | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| **Automatic** (default) | Health Connect when a watch, band, ring or chest strap contributed today's steps, or when Health Connect holds a day this phone never observed. Otherwise the phone. |
| **This phone** | Only what this device's pedometer recorded. |
| **Health Connect** | Whatever your watch and other apps report. |

The picker shows today's phone and Health Connect totals side by side, so the
choice is made between two real numbers rather than two descriptions. Changing it
re-syncs immediately.

Automatic resolves once per day and only ever moves toward Health Connect, never
away from it. The decision is persisted, so it survives the process being killed.

## Health Connect write-back

Opt-in, off by default. Stride can now publish the steps, distance and active
calories it counts, making them available to your other health apps.

- Calories are written as **active**, never total — filing movement-only
  estimates as a total would inflate every other app's basal-inclusive figures.
- Re-syncing a day replaces that day's records rather than appending, so totals
  cannot drift upward.
- Turning it off asks whether to leave the shared data in place or remove it.
  Nothing already shared is deleted without being asked.

## Home-screen widget

New to the open-source edition.

- Four layouts, chosen from the cell you actually give it: a two-cell strip, a
  three-cell row with distance and calories, a square with a goal ring, and a
  larger tile that adds the last seven days as bars.
- Takes its colours from your palette and your light/dark setting.
- Opens the app when tapped.

## Fixes

- **Daily totals can no longer decrease.** The phone's pedometer only counts from
  the moment Stride starts listening; it knows nothing about steps taken before
  installation, before permission, or while the process was dead. It was being
  written in as a correction rather than a floor, which could reset a day's total
  and start it climbing again.
- **Totals are no longer a maximum of two sources.** `max(healthConnect, sensor)`
  selected inflated aggregates whenever two applications logged the same walk.
- **Sensor deltas are correct across reboots and across midnight.** The hardware
  counter resets to zero on boot, and the post-boot cumulative value was
  previously applied as a single delta.
- **Calories are consistent.** Health Connect's total-calorie records include
  basal metabolism, roughly 1,500 kcal of simply being alive, which does not
  belong beside a step count.
- **Days written to Health Connect are no longer one step short**, and reading
  back Stride's own writes no longer compounds them.

## Notes

Requires Android 8.0 or newer. Health Connect is optional; the phone's pedometer
works on its own.

This is the open-source edition under GPLv3. The paid edition adds a GPS walk
tracker, insights, a share studio, streak freezes, coaching, a weekly recap, a
floating step island and two extra skins — none of which are in this repository,
and none of which are needed to count steps.

name: Stride v1.0.3 - Verdant, and steps that go both ways
body: ## 📸 Screenshots ## 🔄 Health Connect: Stride can now write, not just read Stride has always read from Health Connect. It can now publish to it, so the steps, distance and active calories it counts show up in your other health apps instead of staying locked in Stride. It is **off by default**. Settings → Health Connect → *Write steps back*. Turning it on asks for write permission separately from read, and backfills your last 30 days so your history appears rather than only days from then on. A few decisions worth stating plainly: - **Calories are written as *active*, not total.** Stride estimates the energy you burned by moving. Filing that as a total would inflate every other app's basal-inclusive number. - **Re-syncing a day replaces Stride's record for it**, never adds a second one. - **Stride subtracts its own writes when reading.** Health Connect sums every app that writes steps — without this, Stride would read back its own totals as somebody else's and add them again on every sync, and your count would climb on its own. - **Turning it off asks what to do with what you already shared.** Leave it for the apps that are reading it, or remove it. Nothing is deleted silently. ## 🌿 Verdant — a second complete skin Stride already had Classic and the 8-bit Retro skin. **Verdant** is a third: an editorial wellness look — warm off-white ground, olive-lime accents, generous rounded cards, and a dark companion panel. It is not a recolour. Four screens were rebuilt around it: **Today** — the progress ring is gone, replaced by a goal curve. The hero splits into a light stat card beside a dark panel, and every stat carries a sparkline of its own last seven days. **History** — now answers the question the screen exists for: *how does this stretch compare to the last one?* It leads with the period total and a ±% change chip, keeps the bars inside that same card so the number and its shape read as one statement, and follows with an explicit side-by-side comparison. Tap any bar to drill into that day. **Awards** — built on rings rather than bars, so it never reads as another History: your streak drawn against your personal best, a Collection meter with one notch per badge, a ring per challenge, and a badge wall. **Settings** — section names demoted to quiet eyebrows, every row's icon in an accent medallion, a status panel at the top, and the theme picker turned into **visual preview tiles** — each one rendering that skin's actual corner treatment and accent, so you choose a look by looking at it. **The dock** gains a raised centre action that starts a walk. ## 🎚 Theme style One picker, three looks: **Classic · Retro · Verdant**. Existing Retro users are migrated across automatically — nothing to re-select. Classic remains free and completely unchanged. Retro and Verdant are premium. ## 📝 Honest notes - **Huawei Health is not supported.** Huawei watches (GT 2e, GT 3, GT 4, Band) keep their data in Huawei Health, which needs Huawei's own Health Service Kit. That SDK requires an *enterprise* Huawei developer account — individual developers cannot get health scopes at all. The app-side groundwork is done and `docs/HUAWEI_HEALTH.md` spells out exactly what remains, but there is nothing shippable today. If you have a Huawei device and want this, say so on the issue tracker — it helps justify the account. - **Insights** and the **Walk** screen keep their existing layouts. They pick up Verdant's colours and card shapes, but have not had a structural redesign. - Verdant's plant artwork is bundled with the app. ## 📄 Font licence Retro mode uses **Press Start 2P** by CodeMan38, under the [SIL Open Font License 1.1](../OFL-PressStart2P.txt).

name: Stride-v1.0.2-Retro Mode
body: # Stride v1.0.2 — Retro Mode ## 🕹️ Retro Mode Stride now has a full 8-bit skin. Not a recolour — an actual pixel redesign: - **Pixel typeface** throughout (Press Start 2P) - **Stair-stepped corners** on every panel, chip and button — real pixel corners, not small radii - **Chunky outlines** and **hard offset shadows**, the way pixel-art UIs fake depth - **Block progress ring** with a continuous radar sweep - **Blinking terminal caret**, **CRT scanlines**, blocky switches - **Retro map** — the walk map is duotoned into the arcade palette with a pixel frame Toggle it in **Settings → Appearance → Retro mode**. The original Material design is completely untouched behind the switch, and nothing about how the app *works* changes. ## 🎨 Arcade palette A new colour palette inspired by 8-bit tracker consoles: a bright sky-cyan field, deep indigo panels, and coral / mint / amber accents. Light and dark variants. Free for everyone — Retro mode pairs with it automatically. ## ✨ Also new - **Free home-screen widget** — the steps + goal widget is no longer premium - **Background-reliability hint** — if your phone is battery-restricting Stride while background counting is on, the app offers a one-tap fix. This is the single most common cause of "my steps stopped counting" - **Gentle rating prompt** — at most once a fortnight, only after a goal, never again once you've rated - Crash reporting so problems get fixed faster ## 🐛 Fixed - **The goal coach no longer nags.** Dismissing it now sticks for the rest of the day instead of reappearing every time you returned to the dashboard - **Clean midnight rollover** — today's count resets correctly even if the app was never opened around midnight - **Onboarding permissions** are requested in sequence, so prompts are no longer silently skipped - **Accessibility** — the progress ring now reads as one clear label in TalkBack Both share the same package and signing key, so a Gumroad install updates cleanly to the Play build later. ## 📄 Font licence Retro mode uses **Press Start 2P** by CodeMan38, under the [SIL Open Font License 1.1](../OFL-PressStart2P.txt). **Full changelog:** https://github.com/NikhilKain/stride/compare/v1.0.1...v1.0.2

name: Stride v1.0.1
body:
## [1.0.1]

### Fixed
- **Step count accuracy.** The daily total could run ~30% high (one tester saw
  3,831 against a true pedometer reading of 2,906). Stride was blending in Health
  Connect's aggregate, which sums steps from *every* app that writes them (Google
  Fit, Samsung Health, the platform detector…). The on-device hardware pedometer
  is now the single source of truth for the current day; Health Connect is used
  only as a cold-start fallback and for historical days.
- **Calories reflect movement only.** Estimates no longer fold in resting/basal
  energy, so a day with no walking no longer shows phantom calories burned.

### Changed
- **Lighter on the battery.** Step sensor events are now batched (~1s) at the
  hardware layer instead of waking the CPU on every footstep. The count stays
  exact — batched events are delivered, not dropped.

name: Stride 1.0.0
body:
### Fixed
- Stride island could be enabled without a licence via the Live Updates help dialog
- Step count could jump after the app was closed across midnight
- Calories disagreed between the dashboard and history screens
